def lex_min_flip3(s):
    """
    Given a binary string s (characters '0'/'1', 1 <= len(s) <= 200), one
    move chooses an index i with 0 <= i <= len(s) - 3 and simultaneously
    flips the three consecutive characters s[i], s[i+1], s[i+2]
    ('0' <-> '1').  Moves may be applied any number of times (possibly
    zero), in any order, and every window of length 3 is always allowed.

    Return the lexicographically smallest string reachable from s.  All
    reachable strings have the same length as s, and comparison is plain
    dictionary order with '0' < '1' (i.e. usual Python string comparison).
    If len(s) < 3 no move is possible and s itself is the answer.

    The state space has up to 2**200 strings, so enumerating reachable
    states is hopeless; the intended solution exploits invariants of the
    move.

    >>> lex_min_flip3('111')
    '000'
    >>> lex_min_flip3('0110')
    '0001'
    >>> lex_min_flip3('10')
    '10'
    """
